reason: Confirmed in-scope defect (c1): the kernel's precomputed reciprocal MULTIPLIER=2454267026 with SHIFT=34 is not an exact floor-division by 7 over the full uint32 domain. Probe t13 found 4,400 failing values in dense windows near the domain top (Python-level check) and the GPU reproduces them, e.g. index 4294967291 yields row 613566756, col 4294967295 (wrapped negative remainder) instead of col 5; reconstruction 7*row+col fails and col is outside [0,6]. The problem.txt contract explicitly requires EXACT integer decomposition for EVERY uint32 value 0..4294967295 with col in [0,6] and 7*row+col == index, so this is a direct contract violation by legal inputs; no tolerance or alternative-method clause covers it (any division method is allowed only if exactness holds for the whole domain). The GM criterion e*M <= 2^34 holds but only guarantees exactness below ~2^34/e ≈ 3.44e9, not the full 2^32 domain. c2 (Triton 64-bit truncation) is set aside as inconclusive: t10's 286 large-value GPU mismatches are fully explained by the wrong Python-level formula itself, so no separate truncation defect is established and none is needed. c3 (tail/masking) is inconclusive (its only probe was confounded by full-range values hitting the c1 defect; N=1 and N=2 matched), and it adds no failure mode beyond the confirmed c1 defect.
